- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Astronomy is the scientific study of celestial objects and phenomena.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The study includes the sun, moon, planets, asteroids, comets, meteoroids, stars, and nebulae [[1](https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/solar-system/our-solar-system/overview/)].
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The science of astronomy has a rich history that predates other natural sciences such as physics, chemistry, biology, and meteorology.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Astronomy was the first natural science to reach a high level of sophistication and predictive ability [[2](https://www.britannica.com/science/astronomy/History-of-astronomy)].
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Astronomy encompasses various branches that overlap in many directions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The branches of astronomy include Descriptive Astronomy, Practical Astronomy, Theoretical Astronomy, Mechanical Astronomy, Astronomical Physics or Astrophysics, and Spherical Astronomy [[3](https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/asteroids-comets-and-meteors/overview/)].
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] These branches are not distinct and separate; they overlap in all directions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Spherical Astronomy finds the demonstration of many of its formulae in Gravitational Astronomy, and their application appears in Theoretical and Practical Astronomy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Valuable information can be obtained by studying different titles as indicated above.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is important for the student to understand what topics to expect in each branch of astronomy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The science of astronomy studies the nature and constitution, forms, dimensions, and masses of celestial objects, their motions, both real and apparent, the laws which govern these motions, and the effects they produce upon each other by their attractions, radiations, or any other ascertainable influence.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Astronomy is divided into many branches, including Descriptive Astronomy, Practical Astronomy, Theoretical Astronomy, Mechanical Astronomy, Astronomical Physics, and Spherical Astronomy.
